recipes.name: Mexican Beef Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Brown the ground beef in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add chili powder, beans, tomatoes and soup; mix well and heat thoroughly.
Line a 13x9 inch dish with tortillas. Then make a layer with the meat mixture. Make another row of tortillas, then finish off with rest of meat mixture. Top with grated cheese.
Bake in a preheated oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Beef Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Like a giant baked taco! Ground beef with Ranch Style beans and tomatoes on top of corn tortillas, in a cheesy casserole.

review.reviewBody: wasn't sure what ranch style beans were so used kidney beans the first time I made it, adults liked it, kids not so much: the next time I used refried beans,everyone LOVED it. I have made this about 6 times in the last few months since I first tried it. I do add taco seasoning to it as well and the last time I made it, I spread salsa over the top after it was baked..OH MY GOSH, heaven in a pan.Wonderful served with sour cream.Thank you, thank-you

Great recipe! I added 1/2 a pkg taco seasoning to the browned meat. I mixed all ingred together before adding to meat. I used one can Rotel tom with green chillis (do this!) and used 1/2 can refried beans-kept in the chili powder spice-started with meat mix on bottom then layered with cheese-then tortilla-ended with the meat on top - more cheese. Highly recommend doing it this way-so easy. Everything gone so will double next time for left-overs.

the messier a meal is, the better right? My 4 and 6 year old loved this! I made it semi as written...just used what I had in pantry. I had a pound of ground beef that I had already browned, so I needed to do something with it- so this was the lucky recipe. 

Layered bottom of casserole dish with tortilla chips. With my already cooked ground beef, I added a 1/2 pack taco seasoning (white chicken chili mix) can of cream of mushroom soup, a can of rote (untrained), a can of pinto beans (untrained) and a can of corn. Heated all together and began my layering. I covered the top of the casserole with cheddar and mozerella cheese and baked for 20 minutes. 

Once cooled I sprinkled tortilla chips and added a little more cheese (to hide the beans for my kids). Garnished with sour cream and salsa. Quick, easy and delicious. The only thing I would do different-not add so much rotel or taco seasoning ..a little spicy My little girl asked if I will make this again-so definetly a keeper! Thank You!!

I WILL make this again! I did as others suggested. I cooked a med onion with the beef. Drained and I added a full pack of Taco Seasoning. I shredded one 8oz Sharp Cheddar and 1 8oz Monterey Jack cheese. I did use the Ranch Style Beans (that I had never heard of before) and I used Ro-Tel Mexican style diced tomatoes (with Lime and Cilantro). BTW I hate cilantro and this was not overpowering at all. I also added a small can of Green Chillies. I put some of the meat mixture on the bottom and layered the cheese throughout the layers. Each layer took 6 corn tortillas. The leftovers the next day were wonderful.

I’ve made this a few times now and it is delicious! It is also great use for dried out or soggy tortillas and other leftover ingredients. I’ve mixed in rice instead of beans and it works well. I put the beef in the crockpot with salsa or seasoning and then layer the casserole later. I’ve experimented with adding jalapeno slices to the bottom layer or salsa. I serve with salsa so people can choose their spice level and how dry or wet they like it. It tastes great when warmed up days later!

I made this tonight with a few adaptations based on personal preference (we like things spicy!) AND what I had on hand.. I had to sub refried beans for the ranch beans and I kept them separate from the meat mixture. I sautéed half a small onion, diced, with the ground beef and added a packet of low-sodium taco seasoning along with the tomatoes and soup. Tasted it, then added about a cup of medium salsa, a tsp of chile powder, half-tsp of cumin. Then poured a little meat sauce in the bottom of my casserole dish, layered corn tortillas, spread the refried beans over the tortillas, added a bit of shredded cheese, another layer of tortillas & poured all the remaining meat sauce over. Topped it with more shredded cheese & baked as directed. I served it with fresh diced jalapeño, green onion, cilantro & sour cream. Yum! It was a hit!! Thanks for this recipe. I will make it again, soon.

I made this tonight. Everyone liked it. I couldn't find Ranch Beans so I used a Texas blend sold by Bush beans. I did use half the package of taco seasoning like others suggested and added 1/2 cup sour cream to the mixture. Also, I put a light layer of the mixture on bottom of the pan which keeps the tortillas soft. I will be making it again, my husband likes spicy meals and thought it was bland but once he added some hot sauce he liked it. The rest of us at it as is and liked it.

We love this recipe at home but we make it with a twist - taco seasoning and salsa is added and instead of tortillas we add spanish rice to the burger mix and top with crushed up fritos corn chips and then more cheese!!!!!

I liked the basic idea but it definitely needed to be kicked up with more spicy Mexican flavors, which was easy to do. I browned the meat with onions and garlic, then added about a tablespoon of cumin with the chili powder, and used a can of diced fire roasted tomatoes with green chilies, and 2 cups of a bag of pre-shredded blended Mexican cheeses (4 cups is way too much fat!). I also used easy homemade refried beans and handmade corn tortillas from a local shop. I realize the last part isn't feasible for everyone, but they are sooooo much better than corporate-made discs called tortillas.

Used white corn tortillas, taco seasoning instead of chili powder and used 2 lbs of hamburger because we had a potluck to go to. Put some salsa on the top layer then added the cheese. Will definitely make again.

I was hesitant about the mushroom soup, but it worked well for holding the tomatoes&meat together, and tasted great with all the other seasonings. If you didn't know the recipe, you would not think this dish had mushroom soup in it from the taste of it.This was easy and tasted good. Next time around, I will look for ways to reduce salt (prepared beans and soup, plus tomatoes add up to a lot of salt) -- but this is a great recipe for tweaking. I used turkey instead of beef and it tasted great.The casserole looked good and held together when served.
I did what others mentioned and added some cheese between layers. 2.5 cups of cheese was plenty for us, but if you love melted cheese then the 4 cups would be for you.
Somehouw, I ended up with a layer of tortillas on top -- rather than meat mixture-- and it worked fine with cheese atop that. Not messy when served.

This is great comfort food, or Midwestern potluck fare. So easy to make and you can customize to your liking.

Update: made it with leftover thxgiving turkey and it was fantastic. Really nice way to liven up the holiday.
Used ground turkey and taco seasoning, not sure what Ranch beans are, maybe try chili seasoned kidney beans next time. 4 C of cheese is excessive, put cheese between layers and on top.

We Love this ! Its GREAT as written, but who can quit changing things up ? I cook some onions with the beef, add some taco seasoning, substitute "rotel" and add a cheese layer in the middle of layering. I think the Ranch Style Beans Make it - I would definitely not sub these out. Serve with your favorite taco toppings !
This was a big hit. I don't like mushrooms, so I used cream of celery.
I found it to be a bit bland. Would try again with onion and jalapeños.i used black beans, so maybe I'd try Refried like others have. I had to add hot sauce after to jazz it up.
Made one small change. Added a small can of tomato paste.
Hubby LOVES this dish. I add fresh Hatch green chiles he can't get enough. This is a simple delicious regular meal now. Use ranch beans ( this is their name) from walmart.

Fantastic! I love this recipe. Everyone who samples this requests for more. Delicious. I didn't change a thing. I think the ranch style beans add a great flavor to this dish. Added onions to the dish, and it was even better.

I did not have quite enough tortilla chips for the baking pan but I had some Lays potato chips and lined the bottom with Lays and then the meat n cheese as described and then used the tortilla chips above that layer. I also added a small can of green chilis. It came out wonderful! My dog wouldn't leave me alone until a gave him some of it and he wolfed it down, lol! Good recipe to add to the box. I can see it's amost like a cowby caaserole. What you have on hand! I had it all on hand except being short of tortilla chips. Lays worked fine in this pinch.
Liked! Black beans for the beans….whole pkg of Taco seasoning, and took the tip of adding diced onion and garlic to the ground beef….
